children: PortableDoc is Barkpark's block content model — a structured tree of typed blocks that renders identically in the terminal, the web, and the editor.

Long-form body fields on a Document hold a PortableDoc, a tree of typed blocks rather than raw markup. This keeps body content portable across every surface of Barkpark: the same block tree is rendered by Bulldocs on the web, by pdrender in the Go TUI, and edited block-by-block in LiveView Studio.
Each block type carries its own field shape — getting these exact is what keeps Bulldocs and pdrender in parity:
items are arrays of inline-node arrays — each item is itself a sequence of inline runs.
blocks are first-class, so diagrams and recorded terminal sessions live inline in the content rather than as external embeds.
That text-vs-value split between heading and code is a classic parity trap; the renderers must branch on block type, never assume a single key.

PortableDoc is a field type declared via Schema v2 on a Schema, and carried by a Document like any other field. Because it is structured data, Postgres Search can index its text content and the Edge Extractor could in principle mine references embedded in blocks. It is governed by the same Perspective and Workspace + Project scoping as the rest of the Content Model, and is written through a mutation and fetched over the HTTP API v1 like any field — which is exactly how the Bulldocs plugin ingests papers. Because one block tree renders identically everywhere, PortableDoc is the content that ties the Surfaces together.
